answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A knoll of freshly minted accounts then offers no free influence: each bond ties capital to one identity, and provable double-claiming or invalid work burns it. Splitting the attacker’s budget across sybils does not multiply voting weight; it multiplies the capital immobilized and at risk. The timber and onyx labels can identify bond tiers, but the security comes from the costly lock and credible slashing.
